items.claim: The cut inside the pe stanza after 3:47 is byte-warranted by the person shift, but the rejected alternative weighs the stanza it cuts as a tier-3 mark signal instead of the tier-1 letter signal it is.
items.evidence: The person shift the cut rests on is byte-true: the unit runs first-person plural throughout, cohortative נַחְפְּשָׂ֤ה with דְרָכֵ֨ינוּ֙ (oshb:Lam.3.40, byte tier), נַ֤חְנוּ פָשַׁ֨עְנוּ֙ (oshb:Lam.3.42, byte tier), עָלֵ֛ינוּ and אֹיְבֵֽינוּ (oshb:Lam.3.46, byte tier), לָ֖נוּ (oshb:Lam.3.47, byte tier), and turns first-person singular at עֵינִ֔י (oshb:Lam.3.48, byte tier). The defect is the weighing: the alternative is set aside against the stanza's supposed tier-3 parashah-mark symmetry, but the stanza in question is the pe stanza 3:46-48 at letter position 16 of this chapter's pinned pe-before-ayin sequence, a tier-1 text signal; the tier-3 single-witness layer is the mark, and in this chapter marks fall only at stanza ends (22 marked verses of 66; 3:42, 3:45 and 3:48 here), so the mark corroborates the stanza rather than constituting it. A tier-1 stanza is therefore cut against a downgraded counterweight. Second, 3:46 and 3:47 are said to carry plural object suffixes, but their plural elements are one prepositional and two nominal suffixes (עָלֵ֛ינוּ, אֹיְבֵֽינוּ, לָ֖נוּ); the plural verbal object suffixes of the section stand at וַֽתִּרְדְּפֵ֔נוּ (oshb:Lam.3.43, byte tier) and תְּשִׂימֵ֖נוּ (oshb:Lam.3.45, byte tier), outside both verses. Third, holding a verse for the following span is a positional reference to a neighbouring unit rather than a verse-anchored one. Otherwise clean: every Hebrew run collates at byte tier, the four quoted translation lines are verbatim at 3:40, 3:42, 3:46 and 3:47, letters nun, samekh and pe are disclosed, the marks at 3:39, 3:42, 3:45 and 3:48 are disclosed and never conflated with the PE class, and no ketiv/qere note falls inside 3:40-3:47.
tier_citations: tier-1 participant and voice shift (1cp to 1cs at 3:48)
tier-3 weak single-witness parashah mark (22 marked verses of 66 in this chapter)

items.claim: The cross-seam disclosure labels the pe stanza it leaves behind a tier-3 signal, demoting a tier-1 letter stanza; the span's own byte grounds are otherwise sound.
items.evidence: The opening is byte-true: פַּלְגֵי with first-person singular עֵינִ֔י (oshb:Lam.3.48, byte tier) resumes the singular voice after the plural section, and the remaining stanzas are the ayin and tsade stanzas 3:49-51 and 3:52-54, named in this witness's pe-before-ayin order, with חִנָּֽם (oshb:Lam.3.52, byte tier) carrying the without-cause reading the type guess names. The defect: the grouping left behind, the pe stanza 3:46-48, is disclosed as a tier-3 signal, but the letter stanza is the tier-1 text signal in this book; the tier-3 single-witness layer is the mark, and this chapter's marks sit only at stanza ends (22 marked verses of 66; 3:48, 3:51 and 3:54 inside this span). Weighed from both sides, the one seam is argued against a downgraded counterweight on each side, so the mid-stanza exception rests on a tier assignment the bytes do not support even where the exception itself is otherwise warranted. Register residuals: verses argued in the previous span is a positional reference to a neighbouring unit, and the reason offered against it on the other side of the same seam is a cross-unit reference that is not verse-anchored. Otherwise clean: the single Hebrew run collates at byte tier, the quoted translation line is verbatim at 3:48, all three marks in the span are disclosed, and no ketiv/qere note falls inside 3:48-3:54.
tier_citations: tier-1 acrostic letter stanza (pe 3:46-48; ayin 3:49-51; tsade 3:52-54)
tier-1 participant and voice shift (1cs resumed at 3:48)

items.claim: The address-shift seam at 3:55 and the qof and resh stanza span hold on the pointed bytes, with complete letter, mark, quote and disclosure discipline.
items.evidence: The seam rests on a real form shift: 3:52-54 carry no second-person masculine singular element, while this unit opens שִׁמְךָ֙ (oshb:Lam.3.55, byte tier) and runs 2ms suffix-conjugation from there, קָרַ֨בְתָּ֙ and אָמַ֖רְתָּ (oshb:Lam.3.57, byte tier), רַ֧בְתָּ and גָּאַ֥לְתָּ (oshb:Lam.3.58, byte tier). The stanzas are qof 3:55-57 and resh 3:58-60, letter positions 19 and 20 of this chapter's pinned sequence, both entered and completed, so no stanza-boundary exception is needed. The title claim holds: אֲדֹנָ֛י (oshb:Lam.3.58, byte tier) is the only Adonai title inside the span (Adonai: 13 verses book-wide), and the span's other divine-name verses carry the Yahweh name at 3:55 and 3:59 (Yahweh: 32 verses book-wide). The reassurance at 3:57 is reported inside the speaker's own second-person address, not a messenger formula and not a divine-voice frame, so the fabrication class is not tripped; no selah, special letter or paseq is claimed, and no paseq stands in this chapter. Marks: 3:57 and 3:60 are the span's only marks and both are disclosed with the preceding 3:54 named, which is complete symmetry here because this chapter's marks fall only at stanza ends (22 marked verses of 66). All three Hebrew runs collate at byte tier, both quoted translation lines are verbatim at 3:57 and 3:58, no ketiv/qere note falls inside 3:55-3:60, and the confidence and cap posture are consistent with a six-verse two-stanza unit.
tier_citations: tier-1 addressee shift to second-person address at 3:55

items.claim: The closing verbs are labeled imperatives, but 3:64-66 are second-person masculine singular prefix-conjugation forms and the span's one true imperative stands at 3:63, inverting the disclosed discourse ground.
items.evidence: תָּשִׁ֨יב (oshb:Lam.3.64, byte tier), תִּתֵּ֤ן (oshb:Lam.3.65, byte tier) and תִּרְדֹּ֤ף (oshb:Lam.3.66, byte tier) are 2ms prefix-conjugation forms, not imperatives: the tav is the conjugation prefix, which is exactly why the acrostic can place them at letter position 22, and 3:65 carries that prefix on top of the imperative base itself, so the form is unambiguous from the bytes. The translation lines this unit itself quotes render both cited verbs as futures at 3:64 and 3:66, so neither witness supports the imperative label. Meanwhile the span's actual imperative is הַבִּ֔יטָה (oshb:Lam.3.63, byte tier), standing inside the shin stanza the rationale assigns to petition-report; the bare form stands in 2 verses (3:63 and 5:1) with vav-prefixed forms in 2 more (1:11, 2:20) under the single-letter prefix test rather than a blind stripper. The disclosed discourse ground, a shift from petition-report to imperative imprecation beginning at 3:64, is therefore inverted at the form level, and it is the same ground the rejected alternative rests on. The rest is byte-true: shin and tav stanzas at letter positions 21 and 22 close the alphabet; the chapter's single PE mark at 3:66 (1 PE over 66 verses) is kept distinct from the samekh at 3:63 and the preceding 3:60; three Hebrew runs collate at byte tier; both quoted translation lines are verbatim; and no ketiv/qere note falls inside 3:61-3:66.
tier_citations: tier-1 discourse-frame claim tested against the pointed verb forms
tier-3 weak single-witness parashah mark (samekh 3:63; PE 3:66)

items.claim: Both waved-through ketiv/qere flags are refuted: 4:3 is a doubled-note verse, this unit both splices Hebrew from it and quotes its translation with no ketiv/qere disclosure anywhere, and its jackal reading silently adopts one of the two readings.
items.evidence: 4:3 is one of the book's two doubled-note ketiv/qere verses (22 notes over 20 verses), and both notes stand in the source line: ketiv תנין against qere תַּנִּים֙, and ketiv כי ענים against qere כַּיְעֵנִ֖ים (oshb:Lam.4.3; the ketiv forms stand unpointed in the source line and are byte-exact as consonantal skeletons, the pointed qere forms at byte tier). This unit splices בַּת עַמִּ֣י (oshb:Lam.4.3, byte tier) from that verse and also quotes its translation line, and no field carries a ketiv/qere disclosure. The omission is material rather than formal: describing the young as set against nursing jackals reads the plural qere תַּנִּים֙ against the singular ketiv, so one of two competing readings is presented as the text, at the very verse where a recurrence and counting claim is also anchored. Both dispositions treating these as heuristic false positives are refuted. Everything else checks from the bytes: אֵיכָה֙ collates byte tier at 4:1 and the recurrence claim holds, the token standing in 4 verses (1:1, 2:1, 4:1, 4:2) and verse-initial in 3 of them, identical at accent-stripped tier across all four; letters alef through vav are positions 1-6 of this chapter's pe-before-ayin sequence; the two-token phrase test gives 5 verses book-wide (2:11, 3:48, 4:3, 4:6, 4:10), matching the cited digit; every verse of the span carries a mark, each is disclosed as single-witness tier-3, and the preceding PE at 3:66 is named without being conflated with the samekh class; all three quoted translation lines are verbatim.
tier_citations: tier-1 acrostic letter stanza (alef through vav, positions 1-6)
tier-1 eikhah onset at 4:1 (4 verses book-wide, verse-initial in 3)
tier-3 weak single-witness parashah mark (4:1-4:6 samekh; PE at 3:66)
ketiv/qere disclosure layer (22 notes over 20 verses; doubled at 4:3)

items.claim: A translation quote sits unpaired beyond its field's ref window, the named-once claim carries no digit-bearing sweep, and the two-token phrase that straddles the front seam is described as not crossing it.
items.evidence: The quoted line for 4:7 has no translation ref near it: the field's only such ref points to 4:11 and stands 318 characters past the quote's end, outside the proximity window the mechanical pairing uses, so that quote was never bound to a ref by the automatic pass. On my own check it is verbatim at 4:7, so the fact is sound but the quote-plus-inline-ref convention is unmet. Second, the statement that the divine name is named once in this group is an exclusivity claim with no adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming its object and unit. It is byte-true: the Yahweh name stands in 1 of the span's 5 verses, at יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Lam.4.11, byte tier), and in 3 verses of this chapter (4:11, 4:16, 4:20) out of 32 book-wide, while the Adonai title (13 verses book-wide) stands in no verse of this chapter, so the census is unambiguous once stated; as written the object is an English wording rather than a named Hebrew object, and the digit is absent. Third, the two-token bat-ammi phrase stands at 4:6, immediately before this span's front seam, and again at 4:10 inside it (5 verses book-wide: 2:11, 3:48, 4:3, 4:6, 4:10), which is a byte-true device straddling this unit's own seam; saying it frames rather than crosses this boundary denies the straddle that the both-sides seam law requires weighed, and the parenthesis omits its third site at 4:3. Otherwise sound: זַכּ֤וּ (oshb:Lam.4.7, byte tier) is the verse-initial form, letters zayin through kaf are positions 7-11 of this chapter's pe-before-ayin sequence, every verse of the span is marked and disclosed as single-witness tier-3 with the preceding 4:6 named, the second quoted translation line is verbatim at 4:11, and no ketiv/qere note falls inside 4:7-4:11.
tier_citations: tier-1 acrostic letter stanza (zayin through kaf, positions 7-11)
tier-2 cohesion device straddling the front seam (bat-ammi phrase, 5 verses book-wide)
tier-3 weak single-witness parashah mark (4:6-4:11 samekh)
